answer: A timber exchange that forces every agent to post a refundable stake which vests only after verified deliveries resists fake identities: reputation grows trade by trade, like a reef built coral by coral, never poured at once. Spinning up a thousand sock-puppets gains nothing, since each starts at zero trust and must pay the same stake and waiting time; an attacker would have to fund and age a whole dune of idle identities before any of them could move real value, and that upfront cost exceeds what the fraud could earn.
